target_customer: Indian banks, fintechs, investment platforms and gig economy companies that must verify customer identity (KYC)
problem: Physical KYC is slow and costly. After the Reserve Bank of India allowed video KYC in January 2020, companies needed a developer friendly way to run remote identity verification.
product_category: identity verification, eKYC and video KYC

founders.name: Kunwar Raj Singh Sethi
founders.background_notes: YC bio describes B2B founder LinkedIn content with a large audience. Inc42 says the company was founded by former KPMG and ixigo executives but does not say which founder came from which.

founders.name: Sarthak Goel
founders.background_notes: YC bio: computer scientist who coded for an Indian travel marketplace, sold a project to the government.

competitors.name: Signzy
competitors.what: AI based eKYC and video KYC provider

competitors.name: HyperVerge
competitors.what: Identity verification and video KYC provider

technical_complexity.rationale: Document and face verification with machine learning plus video KYC workflows that meet regulator rules. Standard ML engineering for the period, with compliance details as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: At least eight named competitors (Inc42, July 2020) offered similar KYC services, and a developer friendly API was easy to match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bureau Identity acquired inVOID, reported 2023-07-19 by Venture Intelligence citing TechCrunch.

market_need_then: The RBI approved video KYC in January 2020 and Covid pushed remote onboarding. Inc42 (2020-07) reported daily KYCs up to over 15,000 from about 6,000, revenue up 250% in three months and over 50 clients.

branding.domain_note: invoid.co now redirects to bureau.id, the acquirer's site.

rebrands.why: Inedge is the legal entity name per CB Insights, not confirmed as a brand rebrand.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage beyond startup press profiles. The brand was folded into Bureau after the acquisition.

outcome_analysis: inVOID rode the January 2020 RBI video KYC approval and Covid driven remote onboarding, growing fast in 2020 and joining YC in Winter 2021 with more than 35 clients and 5 million KYCs a month claimed. The market was crowded, and the company was acquired by Bureau Identity, reported in July 2023, for an undisclosed price. The YC directory marks it Inactive, which reflects the brand being absorbed, not a documented shutdown. A reported team move to Credenc for a student neobank has conflicting dates.
notes: Directory status is Inactive while sources show an acquisition by Bureau (2023-07), so exit type acquisition is used. A Business Today URL dated 2022-01-20 says inVOID joins Credenc to build a student neobank, while CB Insights dates it January 2026. These conflict with a 2023 acquisition and are unresolved. Funding totals conflict: Village.ai says 1.4M with a 1.2M last seed, CB Insights says 130K. Neither is verified, so amounts are null. Headquarters is Gurugram or New Delhi depending on source.
